title: LoRAHub coefficients from Mirror task code
hypothesis: A development-fitted map from few-shot task support statistics to coefficient-space Mirror coordinates can recover a useful composition of shared LoRA experts with fewer search evaluations than LoRAHub-style coefficient search, at comparable task quality and bytes.
physical_object: shared bank of low-rank linear update experts
mirror_coordinate: few-shot support-derived task code mapped to expert composition coefficients
task: Synthetic few-shot linear regression over 4-dimensional inputs; each task target is a sparse composition of six shared rank-1 experts. Fit coefficient map only on development task identities; evaluate new task identities using 32 support and 128 query examples.

development.selection_metric: Fit a fixed linear support-statistic-to-coefficient map; code dimension and expert count fixed before fresh tasks.

fresh.split: Each fresh world has 12 new tasks with 2-3 expert compositions; 32 support and 128 heldout query examples/task. No fresh task delta used to fit the Mirror map.

success_gate: On >=2/3 fresh worlds, Mirror query MSE <=1.05x direct least-squares fit, beats LoRAHub random search by >=10x coefficient objective evaluations at matched MSE, and actual bytes do not exceed LoRAHub by >5%.
failure_gate: FAIL if quality misses in >=2/3 worlds, if direct coefficient fitting matches Mirror without extra cost, or if search-efficiency gain disappears against the direct least-squares control. Report fresh task code fitting as distinct from end-to-end task training.
boundaries: no language tasks or pretrained LoRA modules
support-statistic code learning is separate from search algorithm
no capacity claim from logical coefficient combinations
